subject: Retention defaults and deletion flow: requests, outputs, and derivative artifacts (Q&A)
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Legal <legal@brightbank.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests, outputs, derivatives)

Hi Karthik,

Quick follow-up from our security review: can you confirm Redwood's default behavior for hosted API calls? Specifically:
- Do you persist the raw request payloads (prompts) and model-generated outputs by default?
- What about derivatives (e.g., embeddings, reranking artifacts, token logs, KV cache snapshots)?
- If data is retained, what is the deletion path and SLA for removal on request?

We're compiling wording for procurement and need clear, customer-facing language. Appreciate a short bulleted answer we can put in our security questionnaire.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Cloud Risk, BrightBank

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests, outputs, derivatives)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a concise explanation below so you can paste into your questionnaire.

Quick bullets (hosted API default):
- Requests (raw prompt/request payload): temporarily stored for 30 days for troubleshooting, quota/abuse detection, and model quality analysis. Customers can opt-out for enterprise plans via account settings or contract.
- Model outputs (generated responses): stored by default for 30 days and then purged; customers may configure longer retention for debugging or compliance under Dedicated/Private contracts.
- Derivatives (embeddings, reranking scores, token-level logs): embeddings and explicit artifacts derived and returned to the customer are stored for 30 days; low-level telemetry (token timing, latencies) is aggregated and retained separately in anonymized form. KV cache snapshots are ephemeral and not written to persistent storage by default.
- Deletion on request: we support account-level purge requests. For hosted accounts, we initiate deletion within 5 business days and the deletion pipeline completes within 30 calendar days for most artifacts (exceptions noted below).

Concise explanation you can use: 
"By default Redwood's hosted API retains request payloads and model-generated outputs for 30 days to support troubleshooting, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. Derivative artifacts (such as embeddings created by API calls) are treated the same by default. KV cache entries are ephemeral and not persisted. Customers requiring shorter windows or automatic non-retention can opt-out in account settings or request a custom contract for Dedicated/Private deployments. Deletion requests are acted upon promptly; initiation occurs within 5 business days and back-end purges finish within 30 days for standard artifacts."

Notes and exceptions:
- Audit logs and billing records are retained longer (90 days to meet operational and billing needs) but do not contain full request/response text.
- For compliance reasons (legal hold), we may be unable to purge some telemetry until the hold is lifted; we'll surface that in any contract.

Putting Marissa on cc to confirm the customer-facing wording and to attach the retention-summary PDF. Laura — could you confirm the deletion SLA wording above is acceptable from ops/legal standpoint?

Cheers,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests, outputs, derivatives)

Sarah — thanks for flagging. Adding a couple clarifying points you might want in procurement copy: 

- "Default capture" = data persisted by our hosted control plane automatically unless the customer chooses a non-capture mode.
- Generated outputs that customers explicitly store via our file/asset APIs are governed by the customer's storage settings (i.e., if they push an output to their S3 integration we don't delete it).
- Embeddings created via API calls are considered "derivatives" and are retained 30 days by default; customers can request immediate purge of derivative indices created by Redwood-managed services.
- KV cache: only in-memory between request hops — never written to disk in the hosted flow.

I attached a short retention-summary PDF that breaks the categories into "ephemeral by default" vs "persisted default 30d." Attaching: retention-summary-30d-v1.pdf.

Marissa Cole
Product Security Liaison, Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-summary-30d-v1.pdf (1 page)

Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests, outputs, derivatives)

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for the summary — a couple of follow-ups from a legal procurement perspective before we finalize contract language:
1) Can you confirm whether deletion requests are irreversible and whether any backups (snapshots) might retain copies beyond the 30-day purge window?
2) Please clarify whether encryption keys managed by customers (KMS) influence retention or deletion timelines (e.g., if keys are revoked, are artifacts still recoverable by Redwood?).

If you can provide two short sentences addressing (1) and (2) we can insert them into our security worksheet and proceed to legal redlines.

- BrightBank Legal

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: BrightBank Legal <legal@brightbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests, outputs, derivatives)

Hi — quick answers for legal copy. Please feel free to paste verbatim into your questionnaire: 

1) Deletion irreversibility and backups: Deletion requests for hosted API artifacts are irreversible for customer-visible artifacts. We maintain short-term internal backups for operational resilience; those backups are also covered by the same deletion pipelines and are purged as part of the 30-day deletion window. In the rare case that a legal hold or disaster-recovery snapshot is created, Redwood will notify the customer and work through the hold process.

2) Customer-managed encryption keys (KMS): If a customer configures a customer-managed KMS key and then revokes access or destroys the key, Redwood cannot decrypt the associated persisted artifacts and therefore cannot recover them. Key revocation is effectively equivalent to making stored artifacts unrecoverable; retention timelines still apply to encrypted blobs, but access is gated by the key.

Action items:
- Marissa: finish the one-page deletion-playbook-stub for procurement (attached).
- Karthik: drop this into the BrightBank security worksheet and confirm done.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
